About this game

Ironclad reproduces Axis & Allies: Global 1940 Second Edition — the full-map WWII grand-strategy board game — with the usability of a modern digital board game and none of the platform overhead.

Rules fidelity

Full Global 1940, by the book

Both the Europe 1940 and Pacific 1940 maps, joined into one board. All six phases with guided, legal-move-only play and undo before the dice.

The whole rulebook is in: the general combat sequence, strategic and tactical bombing with escorts and interceptors, amphibious assault and naval bombardment, AAA fire, carriers and scramble, submarine surprise strike and submerge, kamikaze, blitz, canals and straits, convoy disruption, capital capture, and the split UK economy — one seat with two treasuries and regional capitals at London and Calcutta.

It was built from a chunked, citation-indexed transcription of the official manuals, kept alongside the code.

Engine

An engine you can audit — and dice you can check

The rules engine is deterministic. Given the same state, the same intent and the same dice seed it produces byte-identical output — no Date.now(), no Math.random(), no I/O. Every game is reproducible from its opening position plus an append-only action log, and a replay re-derives the state to catch any divergence.

Dice are rolled server-side from a seeded generator and cryptographically committed before the outcome is computed. The commitment and the disclosed seed both go in the battle log, so any player can check a roll after the fact.

Async play

Play by web. Only the active player needs to be online

Turns can run over days or weeks. The game never stalls waiting for an absent opponent: defenders resolve casualties through pre-set, per-power Defense Profiles — ordered hit-priority lists that also carry standing scramble and kamikaze orders. Set them once, edit them mid-game.

Multiplayer

Accounts, a lobby, and live spectating

Sign in, create or join a game, claim your nations in the lobby, and resume anything in progress. Everyone in a game sees who else is connected — online dots per seat, spectator names, join and leave notices.

Non-players can open any active game read-only and follow it live, moves and purchases and placements appearing as they are staged, including a mirrored battle board during combat. Opt in, per game, to an email when it becomes your turn.

Fog of War

Fog of War

An animated fog covers everything outside your own territory until you can see it — undiscovered, or frozen on its last-seen state. A new Reconnaissance phase and a new unit, the Aerial Reconnaissance Plane (attack 0, defence 1, movement 6). Other aircraft can scout too, but forfeit their turn; recon flights are fired on over AA guns; deployed spies see behind enemy lines.

Espionage

Ironclad Spies

A Reconnaissance phase after Purchase for all espionage. A growable per-power spy pool on its own IPC economy, running sixteen operations across intelligence, counter-intelligence and sabotage — code breaking, interrupt supply chain, sabotage a harbour or an air base, false invasion reports, root out spies, influence neutrals, and more.

Each operation runs an establishment clock, a finish roll, and hostility-keyed escape, capture and kill tables. Everything resolves simultaneously at the end of the round and lands as an intelligence briefing.

Tech

Research & Development

An optional first phase: buy breakthrough dice and roll for sixes. Twelve advances across two charts — heavy bombers, jet fighters, super submarines, rockets, improved shipyards, long-range aircraft, radar, paratroopers and more — tracked with per-power odds and a full history.

Politics

Diplomacy and declarations of war

Per-power war-entry timing and triggers, provoked and unprovoked tracking, the neutral cascade when you cross a true neutral, the Soviet–Mongolian pact, and France’s special rules — no Vichy, a liberation troop bonus.

Goals & powers

Objectives, abilities, elite units

National Objectives give each power bonus income for holding key ground and war-goal conditions, tracked live.

Special National Abilities — seven optional, individually toggled: Banzai Attack, the Hitler assassination gambit, the US National Guard, the Rommel effect, Russian scorched-earth factories, and the Japanese and British home-defence bonuses.

Special Units — eight capped elite units, one per eligible power: SS Panzers, Guards Infantry, Rangers, Commandos, Rikusentai, Bushmasters, Frogmen.

Variants

House rules and alternative scenarios

Set at creation and locked for the game: Rail Movement, Allied Lend-Lease (every transfer draws an Axis-intervention die that can skim or sink it), Economic (IPC) Victory, “Russia, Friend or Foe?”, Infantry Barracks, Submersible Submarines.

Beyond the standard setup and the 1942 opening, two scrambled-team scenarios: West vs East — the Atlantic powers, minus France, against the Pacific bloc — and Eurasian Giants vs Oceanic Empires, the continental land powers against the maritime empires and Japan.

Reference

A rulebook that travels with the game

A searchable, two-pane rules wiki — transcribed and citation-indexed from the official manuals — is one keystroke from the board. Search “scramble” or “amphibious” and read the quick reference without leaving the map.

Art & sound

Painted, not photographed

The board itself stays photographic — it is the scanned physical map, real cartography and real counters. Everything around it is illustrated in an aged 1940s war-poster register: title art, loading screens, battle backdrops, victory and defeat.

The loading and battle art is genuine public-domain poster and painting work from the Library of Congress and Wikimedia, credited on screen. There is an original score, and rulebook tips fill the gaps between turns.

Anywhere

On a laptop, or a phone in landscape

One codebase, one deploy. The layout adapts at runtime down to a phone held sideways, and the whole thing installs as a progressive web app from the browser — no store, no download.

What you need

It runs in the browser. There is nothing to install and nothing to pay.

To play
A current version of Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari. It runs entirely in the browser; add it to your home screen to run it as an app. Best on a laptop, playable on a phone held in landscape.
To join
An invitation. Ironclad is a private game for a small group of friends — new accounts are approved by the owner, and there is no public sign-up.
Built with
React & TypeScript · a tiled Leaflet world map · Node & Fastify · PostgreSQL event-sourcing · WebSockets · a standalone deterministic rules engine.

Ironclad is a fan-made digital adaptation of Axis & Allies: Global 1940, built for private play among friends. It is not affiliated with, licensed by, or endorsed by Hasbro, Avalon Hill or Wizards of the Coast, and has no connection to Steam or Valve. All rulebook text is transcribed for reference only.

Loading and title art: public-domain WWII posters and paintings (Library of Congress / Wikimedia Commons), credited in-app · Page compiled 2026.
